summary: Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat (1894–1991) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Mumbai (MA, 1919) and Harvard (PhD), he held posts at Fergusson College (1932), Visva-Bharati University (~1953–1954), and the University of Delhi (1957–1960).

Purushottama Bilimoria works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. After studying under Shivesh Thakur and earning a PhD from La Trobe University, he held appointments at Deakin University (attested 2001–2009) and the University of Melbourne (attested 2001–2016).
Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891–1973) was an Indology scholar. His career included serving as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and as president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from King's College London in 2014. Kyaw was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow there in 2017.

Péter-Dániel Szántó is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from Balliol College, Oxford, studying under Alexis Sanderson. Szántó held posts at Oxford, All Souls College, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Lin completed an MSc at Fudan University, an MA at the University of Bristol (2004), and a PhD at the University of Washington (2015), supervised by Collett Cox.

Qiang Ning is a historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral research under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. Ning has worked as a researcher at Dunhuang Academy and taught at Yale, San Diego State, and Michigan (attested 2004).

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology who studied under Youwei Kang. He headed the Translation Bureau (1898) and held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China.

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University and earning a PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1982–1986), Duan served as a professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) was a Tibetology and history scholar educated at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. Chen worked at Delingha High School, Qinghai Academy of Social Sciences, and the China Tibetology Research Center (~1993–2010).
Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Zhu held professorships at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree from Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).
R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras (~1980–1990).

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, he worked as a journalist and held long-term positions at Guaranty Trust Company (1928–1934) and J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963).

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian educated at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held teaching and academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1913–1949).
R. N. Gadre was an Indologist who held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University, both attested in 1959.
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1959.

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was an Indology scholar who earned a master's in chemistry from the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He taught at Presidency College, Chennai, the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).
